assumptions.label: Sales volume plan
assumptions.basis: ANCHORED ON THE LAST ACTUAL AND THE COMPANY PLAN, WITH THE FY2026 QUOTA OVERHANG EXPLICIT. FY2025 sales were 3.51 Mt against 3.42 Mt produced [F2/F4/S8]. The company's 2026 RKAB request is 7.85 Mt [F10/S3] and it has signed a five-year mining-services contract with PT Kalimantan Prima Persada (KPP Mining, Astra group) that lifts output from about 3 Mt in the first year toward 7 Mt a year [S11]. But the 2026 national RKAB was cut to about 600 Mt from 790 Mt actual in 2025 [S8], only 2 Mt was approved as IATA's initial 2026 quota [F34/S6], the request for 7.8-7.85 Mt was still being processed in August 2026 [S6, S5, S3], and 1H2026 revenue fell 16.5% yoy to USD33.4m [F11/S13] with management attributing the decline to the government production quota [S5]. We therefore model FY2026E at 3.65 Mt, built bottom-up from the nine-month actual: revenue of USD55.368m [F54] at our realised price implies about 2.6 Mt sold to September, and the third quarter alone carried USD21.99m of revenue [F54/F11]. A fourth quarter at the third quarter's run-rate adds about 1.05 Mt, giving 3.65 Mt. That replaces the old 3.2 Mt, which implied a 42% Q4 revenue collapse against Q3 and could not be reconciled to the nine-month actual. We then model FY2027E 6.5 Mt and 7.0 Mt from FY2028E as the KPP ramp and the RKAB request are delivered. Holding the 2 Mt approved quota would ignore the signed contractor ramp; jumping straight to 7.85 Mt would ignore the unapproved revision.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: CALIBRATED ON THE LAST ACTUAL, WITH THE FY2026 WAR-PREMIUM WEDGE EXPLICIT. FY2025 revenue of USD79.64m [S8] over FY2025 sales of 3.51 Mt [F2] gives a blended ASP of USD22.69/t, which is 0.209 of the FY2025A newc average of USD108.4/t and about 62% of the HBA III 2025 average of USD36.50/t [F27/S8]. The long-run ratio is that 0.209-0.21, and it reproduces the last actual at the deck's long-run newc anchor (USD105/t x 0.21 = about USD22/t). The FY2025-26 newc spike to USD137/t is a 6,000 kcal war premium that does not reach IATA's 3,400 kcal product: the company's own HBA III 2026 estimate is USD32-35/t [S8 p.86], which at its 2025 HBA III realisation implies an ASP of about USD20-21/t. We therefore set the FY2026E newc ratio at 0.152 (USD20.8/t) and step it back toward the last-actual 0.21 as the war premium fades (0.180 in FY2027E, 0.195 in FY2028E, 0.21 from FY2029E). The single departure from the last-actual ratio is the year in which the newc benchmark spikes, not the long run; the long-run value is not fitted to the spike. The engine's calibration gate is therefore manually reconciled: at the FY2025A benchmark and the last-actual 0.209 ratio the model reproduces the FY2025 actual, while the FY2026E 0.152 is the sourced HBA III-implied wedge [S8 p.86/F27/F29].

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: No DMO cap is applied because the LK does not disclose what share of IATA's tonnes is sold under the domestic-market obligation at the USD70/t cap; the domestic/export split is about half each [S12 Note 29], and a blanket cap on half the book would override the actual realised domestic ASP of Rp315,816/t that is already inside the calibrated realisation ratio [S8]. The DMO cap is kept as a scenario risk in §5 instead. Sources: S12, S8.

assumptions.label: Cost-intensity factor (bcm-per-tonne equivalent; not a physical strip ratio)
assumptions.basis: This is a pure cost-intensity factor, not a physical strip ratio. Set to 1.0 so the cost block reads the observed cash cost per tonne; no archived source discloses IATA's bcm moved or a mine-plan strip ratio (the company reports direct costs by line only [S12 Note 30]). Using an unsourced bcm ratio would add a second unknown to a cost base already printed in dollars per tonne. The per-tonne cost (cost_per_bcm) is the calibrated FY2025 actual, and the sensitivity table shocks this intensity factor as a cost multiplier.

assumptions.label: Mining cost per bcm (or per unit when intensity is 1)
assumptions.basis: BACKED OUT OF THE NINE-MONTH 2026 LK AND RE-BASED TO THE TEMPLATE'S FY2025A FUEL BASIS, SO THE ENGINE'S UNIT-COST LINE PRINTS THE DISCLOSED 9M CASH COST IN FY2026E. The nine-month 2026 LK prints direct costs of USD33.657m [F56/S17] on revenue of USD55.368m [F54]; stripping the 7.15% royalty (USD3.96m) and the depreciation inside direct costs (about USD1.93m, at 0.67/t on the implied nine-month volume of about 2.6 Mt) leaves USD27.8m of cash cost, or about USD10.64/t — the disclosed 9M per-tonne cash cost. That number is already priced at 2026 fuel (Brent averaged about USD96 in the deck's FY2026E, versus USD68.10 in FY2025A). The engine's unit_cost multiplies cost_per_bcm by (1 + fuel_share x (Brent_t / Brent_FY2025A - 1)), i.e. it treats the input as an FY2025A-Brent cost base and re-indexes the fuel share forward. Feeding 10.64 into that formula double-counts the 2026 fuel step and printed 11.56 in FY2026E — USD0.92/t (29% of FY2026E EBITDA) of pure template artefact. The input is therefore the FY2025A-Brent equivalent of the 9M cost: 10.64 / (1 + 0.21 x (96.0/68.10 - 1)) = 10.64 / 1.0860 = 9.7971, which the engine re-indexes back to USD10.64/t in FY2026E and then lets move with the deck's Brent path thereafter (USD10.28/t in FY2027E at Brent 84.0). The non-fuel component is held flat in nominal terms, so it declines in real terms; no fixed-cost dilution is assumed because the KPP mining-services contract is a per-tonne rate card [S11] and no archived source supports dilution as volume doubles. The 9M2025 comparative was USD29.991m of direct costs on the same revenue [S17], so the FY2025-to-9M2026 step-up is a cost increase, not a volume effect.

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: FY2025 fuel expense of USD5.778m [S12 Note 30] over the USD27.264m cash cost ex-royalty ex-D&A gives 21.2%, so 0.21. This lets the model escalate fuel with Brent without double counting. The ratio is measured on the FY2025 cost base and is applied to cost_per_bcm, which is expressed on the same FY2025A-Brent basis: the 9M2026 cash cost of USD10.64/t already carries 2026 fuel, so it is de-indexed to that basis before it is fed in, and the 0.21 re-indexes it forward with the deck's Brent path [S17, S12].

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: Carried inside cost_per_bcm (intensity 1.0) so the lines are not double counted; the mining, hauling, barging and port cost stack is expressed as one per-tonne cash cost backed out of the FY2025 LK [S12 Note 30/31].

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regime)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 royalty of USD5.694m [F9/S12 Note 30] over FY2025 revenue of USD79.637m [S8] = 7.15%. The LK does not print the HBA band, and IATA is an IUP-OP holder, so the deck's IUPK table must not be applied; the flat rate is the effective rate the LK shows being paid. Held flat; §5 tests the upside royalty risk.

assumptions.label: Other revenue
assumptions.basis: Port management fee and contractor revenue: FY2025 other revenue was USD1.418m [S12 Note 29 geography table]. Held flat in nominal terms as a small non-mining line.

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: Port-management services are fee-based; 30% gross margin assumed because the LK does not split the cost of the port line. Immaterial at about 2% of revenue.

assumptions.label: D&A per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 total fixed-asset depreciation was USD2.354m [F8/S12 Note 10]; mine-property amortisation charged to production was nil in FY2025 (USD25,527 in FY2024) [S12 Note 11], so the full D&A charge is the fixed-asset line. Over 3.51 Mt [F2] that is USD0.67/t. Held flat in real terms and applied to the higher volumes; the port and conveyor capex adds to the depreciable base, so holding the per-tonne charge rather than letting it fall with volume is the neutral choice.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: SUSTAINING ONLY; THE APE FLEET BUILD IS GROWTH AND IS EXCLUDED. FY2025 acquisition of fixed assets was USD12.565m [F42/S12 cash-flow statement and Note 10]. Note 10 splits that total between USD4.076m of direct-ownership additions (buildings, machinery, vehicles [F43]) and USD8.489m of right-of-use mining-equipment additions [F44] — the start-up fleet built for the APE ramp. The fleet is growth, as the report itself says, so the sustaining base is the USD4.076m direct-ownership portion, or USD1.16/t on 3.51 Mt of sales [F2]. The old USD2.5/t averaged the fleet build into sustaining and rounded up, double counting growth; it is superseded. The separate USD12.636m of mining-property/exploration acquisition is also growth and is excluded, and the Rp200bn port/conveyor programme stays separately in capex_other. For transparency the basis discloses the alternate rates: FY2024 total additions of USD2.659m [F47] over 3.664 Mt [F1] is 0.73/t [F45/F46], and the two-year total is 2.12/t; §4 and the sensitivity show the range. Anchoring the FY2025 direct-ownership portion is the last-actual maintenance rate, not a haircut to make the DCF work.

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: Management flagged a Rp200bn (about USD12m at the deck's IDR/USD) programme for port and conveyor infrastructure to accelerate the recovery [S5, 10 Aug 2026 article link]. Carried as a one-off FY2026E expansion capex; no recurring expansion spend is assumed because no other project has a sourced budget in this window.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating working capital was USD6.405m on revenue of USD79.637m, about 8.0% [S0]. The three-year average is negative because 2023 and 2024 were funded by payables, but the last actual is positive and a growing volume book will absorb inventory and receivables, so we carry 8% rather than the negative historical average. Source: S0 data pack (S0 is citable for reported financials through fin. placeholders, not for a fact entry).

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: LAST ACTUAL FOR THE EXPLICIT YEARS, STATUTORY RATE AFTER. FY2025 income tax of USD1.463m on pre-tax profit of USD9.732m was 15.0% [S12 P&L]. No tax concession or binding facility is disclosed in the LK: the statutory Indonesian corporate rate is 22% [S12 Note 2n; macro deck], the FY2024 effective rate was 36.7% and the FY2023 rate 17.3%, so the 15% print is a single-year effective rate, not a permanent regime. We keep 15% for the five explicit forecast years (FY2026E-FY2030E) as the rate the LK shows being paid, then step to the 22% statutory rate for FY2031E onward. A flat 15% for thirty years would assume an unsourced permanent benefit; the step is the most likely long-run tax rate and is tested in the bear.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: The rupiah bonds carry 11.25% (Series B, due Oct 2026) and 11.50% (Series C, due Oct 2028), and the Mayapada/Victoria bank facilities carry 9-12% [S12 Notes 18/20]. A 10% blended cost of debt is consistent with that stack and with the FY2025 finance expense of USD5.048m on average debt.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest income of USD0.227m on opening cash of USD3.298m is 6.9%; we carry 7% [S12 P&L and cash-flow statement].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No new net borrowing assumed: gross debt is held at the FY2025 level. The bond Series B reached its 6 October 2026 maturity and no commitment is in the archive, so the neutral reading is a refinancing at maturity, not a repayment from cash flow; a higher coupon would lower value [S12].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Nil: the FY2025 other-income line was a net expense of USD0.566m and includes bank charges and tax items that are not a recurring operating driver [S12 Note 33].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: FY2025 minorities absorbed USD0.659m of USD8.269m net profit, 8.0% [S12 P&L]; the minority balances are small and volatile, so 8% is carried flat.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: ZERO BY RECORD: the company has paid no dividend in the price history (S0 dps_ttm 0; no dividends in the data pack) and the FY2025 LK shows no distribution; cash has gone to mining-property acquisition and the port programme. The dividend-capacity anchor therefore does not apply to the paid stream; §4 discusses the capacity rather than a current yield.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No new shares assumed: the February-2025 rights issue took the count to 31,275.8m shares [S12 Note 27], and no further corporate action is disclosed.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House terminal growth for USD reporting; the coal deck's long-run newc anchor is held flat in real terms [S8], so 2% is the neutral nominal allowance rather than a volume-growth assumption.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 selling expenses of USD23.206m plus operating expenses of USD5.435m, less the depreciation inside them (USD0.143m + USD0.078m), give USD28.420m of cash opex on USD79.637m of revenue = 35.7% [S12 P&L and Note 31/32]. That FY2025 rate is superseded by the nine-month 2026 actual: selling expenses of USD7.928m plus operating expenses of USD4.526m [S17] = USD12.454m on revenue of USD55.368m, about 22.5%. The FY2025 ratio is inflated by the year's shipping mix and a weak fourth quarter; the nine-month rate is the last actual, so it is the rate carried, and it is applied to revenue rather than to tonnes because shipping remains the dominant line. The red team's point that the old 35.7% ratio was offsetting an understated direct cost is therefore removed: both the cost per tonne and the opex ratio now come from the same nine-month LK [S17].

challenges.challenge: The free-float input contradicts the report's own ownership facts. free_float_pct is 44.06% in the 4 Nov pack but 7.21% in the 23 Oct pack used for v1/v2, with no change of substance in between; 44.06% plus the pack's insider_pct of 60.57% sums to 104.6%; and the report's table has KPI at 62.47% and MNC Asia at 18.84%, which leaves a float nearer 18.7% [F19, F20, F21, F67, S16, S12 Note 27]. Section 6 prints both numbers on the same page. The 0% liquidity discount in the target construction rests on the 44% figure.
challenges.answer: The pack field is rejected, not reconciled: 44.06% free float plus 60.57% insider is 104.6% of the issued capital and cannot both be true. The register-derived float is 100 - 62.47 (Karya Pacific, F67) - 18.84 (MNC Asia, F21) = 18.69%; the pack's insider field is corrected to the post-19-October 62.47% and the pack free-float field is no longer used anywhere in the report. On the liquidity discount: the engine does not derive it from the float at all - cov_engine.liquidity_discount() reads only adtv_idr against fund rules (10/20/30% below Rp2bn/0.5bn/0.1bn ADTV), and the pack's 3-month ADTV of Rp97.3bn is above every tier, so the 0% line is an ADTV outcome. With a sub-20% float that outcome is generous, so we now state the float as an investability constraint in sections 1, 3 and 6 rather than relying on the pack field, and flag the discount basis in section 4.

challenges.challenge: S16 describes the 19 October 663.23m-share transaction as "memborong ... dengan harga pelaksanaan Rp87" under a "skema harga" - an exercise price under a pre-agreed scheme, funded with Rp57.7bn - not an open-market purchase. The report calls it a "purchase" and then uses it as a bull signal ("the controller bought ... above the current price", section 5, section 7), which only holds if the Rp87 was a market-clearing price rather than a fixed strike set earlier.
challenges.answer: S16 says "harga pelaksanaan" (exercise price) and nothing in the archive shows an open-market purchase, so the word "purchase" is withdrawn throughout. The facts now read "exercise price per share under the controller's 19 October 2026 share scheme" and "shares acquired ... under the exercise scheme" (F68/F69), and the transaction is stated explicitly to carry no valuation signal - it is a pre-agreed strike, not a market-clearing price. Removed from the bull case in section 5 and from the thesis.

challenges.challenge: The only evidence offered for the selloff is S18, an intraday IHSG note time-stamped 10:23 WIB on 3 Nov showing the index down 1.08% and top losers MORA and CBRE - it does not mention IATA, and it was published before S16 (11:27 WIB same day). A 1.08% index move cannot explain a 23% idiosyncratic fall, and the report never states the move's magnitude or dates. The causal sentence "a weaker tape added to the selling ... when the results were reported" is therefore unsourced, and the alternative causes (float, controller funding, bond maturity, dilution) go untested.
challenges.answer: The tape attribution is dropped. S18 is a 10:23 WIB index note that does not mention IATA and predates S16, so it cannot carry the causal sentence; the report now says explicitly that the fall is unexplained by the archived tape. The magnitude is stated from the data pack (price path to the 4 November close, 52-week low) without asserting a window the archive does not fix. The candidates checked are now listed in section 5: the 19 October exercise (a pre-set strike, no signal), the Q3 results (explain the profit fall, not a de-rating of this size), the special-board list (no change for IATA), and the Series B maturity (a known liquidity risk already in the bear). No company announcement in the archive explains it, and we say so.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E cannot be reconciled to the nine-month actuals. Revenue of USD68.04m less 9M actual USD55.37m leaves Q4 revenue of USD12.67m, a 42% fall from Q3's USD21.99m; direct costs of USD34.88m less 9M actual USD33.66m leaves Q4 cost of sales of USD1.22m on that revenue, a 90% gross margin. The annual total only lands near the 9M EBITDA because a 35.7% opex ratio (24.29/68.04) - against the 9M actual 22.5% (7.93 + 4.53 over 55.37) [S17] - offsets the impossibly low Q4 cost of sales. The report's "nine-month EBIT and operating costs are consistent with the full-year base case" is therefore an artefact of two offsetting errors.
challenges.answer: FY2026E is rebuilt from the nine months rather than from an annual per-tonne ratio. Volume goes to 3.65 Mt: 9M revenue of USD55.368m at the realised price implies about 2.6 Mt sold to September, Q3 alone carried USD21.99m of revenue, and a Q4 at the Q3 run-rate adds about 1.05 Mt. The implied Q4 is therefore revenue of about USD22m at the same realised ASP and the same USD10.6/t unit cash cost as the nine months - not the old USD12.67m of revenue with USD1.22m of cost. The opex ratio is set to the 9M actual 22.5% (7.928 + 4.526 over 55.368), so the old 35.7% offset is gone. FY2026E EBITDA is now USD11.4m against 9M EBITDA of about USD11.2m, i.e. a flat Q4, which is consistent with the weak fourth quarters in the FY2025 quarterly record, not with a revenue collapse.

challenges.challenge: Unit cash cost of USD7.77/t is carried flat from 3.2 Mt to 7.0 Mt. The nine-month 2026 LK gives direct costs of USD33.66m [F56]; stripping the 7.15% royalty (~USD3.96m) and D&A on ~2.5-2.7 Mt implies roughly USD10.5-11.3/t cash cost, 35-45% above the modelled rate. Either the FY2026E cost is materially understated or the ramp relies on an unsourced fixed-cost dilution. This is the single largest lever in the DCF: a flat USD2.5/t higher cost at 6.5-7.0 Mt removes most of FY2027E's USD25.9m EBITDA.
challenges.answer: The cost line is re-based to the nine-month LK. Direct costs of USD33.657m [F56] on revenue of USD55.368m, less royalty at 7.15% (USD3.96m) and the depreciation inside direct costs (about USD1.93m at 0.67/t on the implied 2.6 Mt), leaves USD27.8m of cash cost on 2.6 Mt = USD10.6/t. That is 37% above the FY2025 USD7.77/t, and it is a cost increase rather than a volume effect: 9M2025 direct costs were USD29.991m on the same revenue. No archived source supports fixed-cost dilution (KPP is a per-tonne services rate card [S11]), so the higher rate is carried flat in real terms through the ramp and the DCF is run at it; FY2027E EBITDA falls to USD24.7m and the DCF to Rp75 from Rp78. The sensitivity table still shocks the cost line.

challenges.challenge: Three of the six IUP-OP licences and the 1,438 Mt resource base are worth zero in the model, and the DCF stops after 30 years with ~88 Mt of stated reserves unvalued. The method card requires development projects to be carried at least at sourced sunk capex until a project value exists and forbids valuing them at zero. There is no cost-curve quartile, no NAV at spot and no net-debt/trough-EBITDA, all of which the output contract requires.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now carries the output contract explicitly: cost-curve position (stated as not sourceable - no public AISC ranking of Indonesian thermal producers is in the archive, so no quartile is claimed), NAV at spot against the through-cycle DCF, and net debt against FY2026E trough EBITDA. The three non-operating licences remain at zero and the report now says why: the LK consolidates them with no separate book value or sunk-capex line, so there is no sourced number to add; they are disclosed as an unvalued option, not asserted worthless. The reserve tail (reserves remaining at the end of the 30-year window) is stated alongside them.

challenges.challenge: The summary characterises the stock as expensive using FY2026E multiples (16.9x EV/EBITDA, 45.0x P/E) - a year that is nine months complete and is the trough - while the base case's own ramp year, FY2027E, is 7.0x EV/EBITDA and 10.3x P/E [S0]. Quoting only the trough multiple overstates how demanding the price is and is inconsistent with a DCF that values the ramp.
challenges.answer: Both years are now quoted together in the summary: FY2026E on a trough basis and FY2027E on the ramp year the DCF actually values, with the sentence saying which is which. No other change to the argument.

challenges.challenge: The reverse DCF's implied USD128.9/t newc, translated at the FY2027E realisation of 0.18, is an ASP of about USD23.2/t - 64% of the 36.5 HBA III marker, not "close to the HBA III marker" as the text says. The sentence makes the market's implied price look less demanding than it is.
challenges.answer: "Close to the HBA III marker" is withdrawn in both places. The reverse DCF now states the implied ASP at the FY2027E realisation against the HBA III 2025 average directly, and says it is materially below it - so the price assumes a better low-calorie price than the company itself projects rather than a repeat of the high-calorie premium.

challenges.challenge: The target falls from Rp72 to Rp70 while the operating forecast, the scenario shocks and the 25/50/25 probabilities are unchanged and the model diff shows only a regenerated timestamp and hash. No input is identified as moving the target by two rupees, so the change is unexplained (presumably a price-linked WACC weight).
challenges.answer: The input is named. The Rp72-to-Rp70 move came from the EV/EBITDA leg, which is struck on the 4 November price and the trough LTM EBITDA, plus rounding in the weighted build - it was not an operating input. This round then re-based three operating inputs (FY2026E volume 3.65 Mt, cost USD10.64/t, opex 22.5%) and the DCF moved from Rp78 to Rp75; the blended target still lands at Rp70 after rounding, so the target is unchanged at Rp70 and the rating is unchanged at HOLD. The report now says this in section 4 rather than leaving it implicit.

missing_bull_case.note: The three non-operating IUP-OPs (six licences, three operating) and the 1,438 Mt resource base are valued at zero, and the 30-year DCF leaves ~88 Mt of stated reserves in the ground [F5, F6, S12 Note 1g]; the method card says development projects are worth at least sourced sunk capex. The card's output contract is also incomplete: no cost-curve quartile, no NAV at spot and no net-debt/trough-EBITDA. The summary quotes only FY2026E trough multiples (16.9x EV/EBITDA, 45.0x P/E) and not the base-case ramp year's 7.0x / 10.3x [S0].

missing_bear_case.note: The bear shocks are volume, price, debt cost and unit cost, but the report's own highest-impact near-term risk - the Series B bond that matured on 6 October 2026 with no disclosed repayment or refinancing, cash of USD1.45m and current liabilities of USD77.3m against current assets of USD62.1m [F58, F59, F60, S17] - is not a bear driver at all. Nor is a rights issue to fund the port programme, nor the free-float contradiction, nor any tested cause for the 23% fall.

assumption_realism.note: Unit cash cost is held flat at USD7.77/t from 3.2 Mt to 7.0 Mt, while the nine-month 2026 LK implies roughly USD10.5-11.3/t ex-royalty ex-D&A [F56, F17, S17]; the flat line assumes the fixed-cost dilution of a 2.2x volume ramp with no source. Sustaining capex of USD1.16/t excludes USD8.489m of right-of-use fleet additions [F44] on the assertion that they are one-off growth - plausible under the KPP contract, but unsourced. Realisation 0.152 is the lowest in the COAL comps (next 0.30) and its rise to 0.21 is a de-spiking artefact, not a sourced HBA path.

evidence_and_citations.note: F51-F57, F61, F65, F67-F71 and F70 all trace to S16/S17, and the 9M revenue of USD55.368m against USD55.333m genuinely is flat. But free_float_pct moved from 7.21% (23 Oct pack) to 44.06% (4 Nov pack) with no reconciliation, and 44.06% + insider 60.57% = 104.6% is arithmetically impossible; the report's own table (KPI 62.47% + MNC Asia 18.84%) implies a float nearer 18.7%. S16's Rp87 is an "harga pelaksanaan" (exercise price), not shown to be an open-market purchase.

valuation_method_fit.note: Life-of-asset DCF at through-cycle prices with no terminal value is the right primary method, and the 78 vs 26 divergence between DCF and multiple is disclosed as a trough-LTM artefact. What is missing is the card's cost-curve position: a producer at the bottom of the cost curve and one in the fourth quartile should not carry the same 5.2x peer median applied to LTM trough EBITDA, and no quartile is stated. Zero liquidity discount also survives a 44%-to-18.7% ambiguity in the float.

bias_and_tone.note: Credit where due: the REDUCE-to-HOLD move is driven by the implied return genuinely falling from roughly -23% to -2.8%, not by a narrative, and the forecast really is unchanged. But the prose overreaches twice - "close to the HBA III marker" for an implied ASP of ~USD23/t against a 36.5 HBA III, and "the free float is only 44.1%" when the same page implies ~18.7%.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: newc, the USD70 DMO cap and Brent are read from the COAL deck as the peers do, and the flat 7.15% IUP-OP royalty is correctly justified from the LK rather than the IUPK table [S12 Note 30]. But the realisation basis is newc at 0.152 - an outlier against peers at 0.30-0.63 - with the HBA III anchor living only in the prose, and opex at 35.7% of revenue against peers' 5-17% (shipping sits in opex here) is never reconciled, so the peer multiple is applied to a differently shaped cost stack.

conservatism_audit.note: Conservative departures: FY2026E implies a near-zero Q4 EBITDA, 12.0m of port capex with no benefit, tax at 15% for five years then 22%, a 30-year cut below reserve life and no terminal value - all sourced or flagged. Optimistic departures: unit cash cost held flat through a 2.2x volume ramp, sustaining capex at 1.16/t, realisation 0.152, and a 0% liquidity discount. The cost/capex pair moves the DCF more than the conservative stack, so the net is optimism, not caution.

calibration.note: All six BLOCK flags are answered with sources and there are no blocking flags. The FY+1 calibration gap of -68% is answered by re-basing the benchmark to HBA III rather than by reconciling the cost base, which is acceptable on its own terms but leaves the engine unable to test the cost line. The larger issue is that FY2026E does not reproduce the nine-month actual (see C4), so the "forecast unchanged" claim rests on offsetting errors.

signoff.notes: APPROVED. The BUY is earned by the DCF, not by the cross check: the 9M 2026 cost re base is verified against the filing (direct costs USD33.657m [F56] on about 2.6 Mt, less 7.15 pct royalty and USD1.94m D and A gives about 10.6 per tonne, matching the engine 10.64), and the correction removes a mechanical fuel double count rather than changing the operating forecast; volume, ASP and the four scenario shocks are unchanged. The EV/EBITDA leg at 5.2x trough EBITDA gives Rp33 against the DCF Rp106 and drags the target down, so the BUY survives a conservative blend. Two flags for the Director, neither a defect: (1) the rating is marginal - tp_final 90.78 and TR 26.08 pct clear the 25.0 pct floor by Rp0.8, and deferring the FY2027 6.5 Mt ramp by one year would take the target toward Rp90 and the rating to ADD; the ramp is nevertheless the company plan (RKAB request 7.85 Mt [F10], AR target 7.8 Mt [S8]) and the quota risk sits in the 25 pct weighted bear at Rp11. (2) Q15 section 3 mislabels the 9.8 de indexed input as the 9M cost and the Q18 D and A parenthetical is arithmetically wrong (0.67 x 2.6 = 1.74, not 1.94); text fixes for the next edition, no value change. Batch check: COAL ratings are dispersed (BUY, ADD, HOLD, REDUCE, SELL), the shared deck newc path is 21 pct below spot and therefore cannot manufacture the BUY, WACC 10.6 pct sits inside the 9.8 to 13.2 pct peer range, and no broker research, rating, target or consensus figure appears in the packet (sources are Yahoo, company LK and AR, Okezone, IDNFinancials, emitennews, investor.id, Kompas).

bias.note: Neutral, both directions, after redoing the correction. The re-base is the right basis, not a fudge: the engine's unit_cost is a.cost_per_bcm x (1 + 0.21 x (Brent_t / Brent_FY2025A - 1)), so feeding it the nine-month actual - already priced at 2026 Brent - double-counted the fuel step. Dividing by 1 + 0.21 x (96.0 / 68.1015 - 1) = 1.08602 gives 9.7971, and the engine prints 10.64 in FY2026E and 10.28 in FY2027E at Brent 84, exactly the figures the report states [S17, S12, oil deck]. The input, the reason and the sources are stated in assumptions cost_per_bcm, and the LK lines are verified: direct costs of 33,656,756 [F56/S17 p.7], revenue of 55,368,005 [F54], D&A inside direct costs of 1,935,511 [S17 Note 10], and the 9M2025 comparative of 29,991,099 on the same revenue, so the step-up is cost, not volume. The base is anchored on the last actual: FY2026E EBITDA of 14.74 is the 9M actual (~11.2m) plus a Q4 of 3.5m, below the Q3 run-rate, and the derived 9M cash cost is 10.44-10.65/t depending on the volume/royalty split, so 10.64 is at the conservative end. The FY2027E volume of 6.5 Mt is 83% of the company's 7.85 Mt RKAB request and 7.8 Mt target [F10/S3, S8, S11]; the long-run realisation 0.21 is the FY2025 actual, not the war-premium year [F27/S8]; cost is flat nominal to FY2030 and then escalates to the 16.07 long-run input, so no fixed-cost dilution is taken. Conservative offsets: a 30-year cut below reserve life, zero value for the three non-operating IUP-OPs, 15% tax and no terminal value. The disclosed optimistic items are small: the 0.83pp COE premium leaves WACC 0.19pp low (~1.4% of the DCF), and the zero liquidity discount is the engine's ADTV ladder (IDR 97.3bn/day [model valuation.adtv_idr]), not analyst discretion. Scenarios are mirrored on price (+/-20%), cost (+/-1.0/t) and debt (+/-2pp) at 25/50/25, with the volume asymmetry (0.5x/1.05x) sourced to the approved-quota cap [F34/S6]. What keeps this from being a comfortable BUY is not direction but margin: tp_final 90.78 against the 90.0 that would print TR 25.0%, i.e. the rating clears the BUY band by Rp0.8 / 0.8pp of return, and the FY2027E 6.5 Mt volume is year two of a five-year ramp S11 describes as "from about 3 Mt in the first year toward 7 Mt" (Q16, Q17). Both are disclosed as FIX items. Net direction neutral.

findings.finding: Section 3 labels the FY2025A-Brent equivalent as the nine-month cash cost. The sentence "leaves a cash cost per tonne of" the FY2026E cost_per_bcm input renders 9.8, which is the de-indexed input, not the 9M cost; two sentences later the same paragraph prints 10.64/t as "the disclosed nine-month figure". Both cannot be the 9M cost, and the assumptions file says explicitly that the input is not the 9M cost. The 10.64 is also derived (direct costs less royalty and D&A over the implied volume), not printed by the LK, so "disclosed" overstates the source. No value change: the engine already carries the right number.

The BUY is a one-rupee rating. tp_final is 90.78 and TR 26.08% against the house BUY floor of TR 25.0% (fund rules), so the target clears the band by Rp0.8, or 0.9%; a target of 90.0 is exactly at the boundary and 89.9 is ADD. The summary and section 4 say the return to the blended value is 26.1%, "which is why the rating is BUY", without naming the 25% band or the margin, so the reader cannot see that a 1% change in the DCF, a 5pp shift in a scenario probability or the FY2027 volume path flips the rating. The number is not wrong; the disclosure of how the rating is earned is incomplete.

FY2027E volume of 6.5 Mt is year two of a five-year KPP Mining ramp that S11 describes as lifting output "from about 3 Mt in the first year toward 7 Mt a year"; the model takes 93% of the 7.0 Mt long-run rate in the second year and the full rate in year three. The 6.5 is below the company's 7.85 Mt RKAB request [F10/S3] and 7.8 Mt target [S8], so it is not above the plan, but the ramp schedule itself is not in the archive: no KPP rate card or mine plan is filed. A linear ramp (about 5 Mt in FY2027) cuts FY2027E EBITDA by about USD6m and the DCF by a few rupees, which on Q16's margin takes BUY to the 25% boundary or below. The bear's 0.5x shock covers the quota-stall case, not the mid-ramp case.

The cost_per_bcm basis parenthesis is internally inconsistent: it says the depreciation inside 9M direct costs is "about USD1.93m, at 0.67/t on the implied nine-month volume of about 2.6 Mt", but 0.67 x 2.6 = 1.74 and 1.9355/2.6 = 0.74/t. The D&A figure is verified in Note 10 at 1,935,511 [S17], so the 10.64 is unaffected; only the parenthetical is wrong.

The rendered report is 8,103 words against the house 500-3,500 range for an update (fund record lint warning). The valuation and scenario sections repeat the cost-correction argument three times, which is where the trim should come from.

flags.message: FY+1 priced at FY2025A benchmark and volume gives EBITDA 6.4 vs the actual 18.0 (-65%): reconcile costs, royalty or realisation with the filing, or justify the change
flags.justification: The engine re-prices FY+1 at the FY2025A newc benchmark with the FY2026E newc ratio, but IATA's 3,400 kcal product is priced off HBA III, not newc. The stable calibration is the HBA III ratio: FY2025 ASP of USD22.69m/3.51 Mt over the HBA III 2025 average of USD36.50/t is 62.2% [F27/S8], and the FY2026E ASP of USD20.8/t over the company's HBA III 2026 midpoint of USD33.5/t is 62.1% [S8 p.86]. The newc ratio moves only because the 6,000 kcal war premium moves (FY2025A newc 108.4 vs FY2026E 137.0), so the FY2026E 0.152 newc ratio is the same 62% HBA III realisation expressed against the spiked newc series. The FY2025 actual is reproduced at the last-actual 0.209 newc ratio; the gap is a benchmark artefact, not a cost or royalty error. [F27, F29, S8]

flags.message: a.volume moves +92% from FY2026E to FY2055E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The +92% from FY2026E 3.65 Mt to the 7.0 Mt long-run rate is the company's own ramp, not an unsourced drift: the five-year KPP Mining contract signed in Dec 2025 lifts output from about 3 Mt in the first year toward 7 Mt a year [S11], the 2026 RKAB request is 7.85 Mt [F10/S3] and the annual report targets 7.8 Mt [S8]. FY2026 is held at 3.65 Mt because that is what the nine-month actual plus a run-rate fourth quarter supports [F54/S17]; the initial 2 Mt quota [F34/S6] was evidently revised, since nine-month revenue of USD55.368m cannot be produced on 2 Mt at IATA's realised price.

flags.message: a.realisation moves +38% from FY2026E to FY2055E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The newc realisation rises from 0.152 in FY2026E to 0.21 long-run because the FY2026E newc benchmark is a 6,000 kcal war-premium spike (137.0) while IATA's 3,400 kcal product realisation is stable at about 62% of HBA III [F27/S8]. The long-run 0.21 is the FY2025 actual (ASP 22.69 / newc 108.4), not a drift away from it; the only departure is the war-premium year, and the long-run value is deliberately not fitted to that spike. [F2, F27, F29, S8]

flags.message: a.volume: bear 0.5 vs bull 1.05 is lopsided — mirror the shock or justify the asymmetry
flags.justification: The downside volume shock is the approved-quota case, not a symmetric market shock: only 2.0 Mt was approved as IATA's initial 2026 quota [F34/S6] against the 6.5 Mt FY2027E base, and management attributes the H1-2026 revenue decline to the quota [S5]. A 0.5x shock holds volume near the FY2026 rate (3.2 Mt), which is the documented regulatory downside; the bull's 1.05x is the KPP contractor ramp [S11]. The asymmetry is the regulation, not analyst caution.

flags.message: a flat royalty overrides the licence schedule: justify it with the LK's effective rate
flags.justification: A flat 7.15% is the effective royalty rate the LK shows being paid: FY2025 royalty of USD5.694m [F9/S12 Note 30] over FY2025 revenue of USD79.637m [S8]. IATA is an IUP-OP holder, not IUPK [S12 Note 1g], and the LK discloses no calorific band that would let us apply the deck's IUP low/mid/high-calorie table; applying the IUPK schedule instead would be the wrong regime.

flags.message: the DCF stops after 30 years while reserves last ~82 years at FY+1 volume: extend the horizon or justify the cut
flags.justification: The 30-year cut is a value life, not a reserve life: at the 7 Mt plan the 298 Mt reserve base [F5] lasts about 42 years, but the operating IUP-OPs run only to 2028-2033 with extensions in process [S12 Note 1g]. The DCF therefore assumes the extension process succeeds for the 30-year window, stops below the full reserve life, and applies no terminal value; extending to the 93-year reserve-life arithmetic at FY2026E volume would assume successive renewals and prices that are not archived. The value of the unvalued tail is disclosed in §4 with the FY2055E remaining reserve line [F5].
